reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be a complete finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure, and let m be any natural number, with nodes Fin(m). Let V:E->R be C^2 and let kappa be a nonnegative real with 1<=kappa. Assume, for every x,v in E,
  kappa^(-1)||v||^2 <= D^2 V(x)[v,v] <= ||v||^2.
Fix eta,c,epsilon in R satisfying 0<eta<=c<1 and epsilon>0. Let nu be a probability measure on E x E and let xstar in E satisfy grad V(xstar)=0. Fix h,M,S>=0. Assume (X,P)->||X-xstar||^2+||P||^2 is integrable under nu with integral <=M. Let t:Fin(m)->R satisfy |t_i|<=1, and omega:Fin(m) x Fin(m)->R satisfy sum_j |omega_ij|<=S, for every i. Let b,d:Fin(m)->R be arbitrary, denoting positionWeight,momentumWeight.
Write D=dim_R E, a=exp(-h/2), sigma=sqrt(1-exp(-h)), G for the centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability law on E, gi=product_{Fin(m)} G, gamma=(G x G) x (gi x gi), and mu=nu x gamma. Under mu the incoming state is independent of all noises, while the two single-vector noises and the two independent finite Gaussian arrays are mutually independent. Set exactly
  MR=M+(1-exp(-h))D,
  B=6 MR+3 epsilon^2+3 eta D,
  C=2+(1+log((1-c)^(-1)))/(-log c),
  L0=C[1+log(1+sqrt(2 MR)/epsilon)],
  L1=C[1+log(1+sqrt(4 MR+2 S^2 B)/epsilon)].
Then there exist global measurable functions p,q:E->E and N:E->N such that for every y,
  p(y)+eta grad V(p(y))=y,
  ||q(y)-p(y)||<=epsilon,
  run(grad V,eta,epsilon,y,N(y)+1,y)=some(q(y),N(y)+1).
The exact-real interpreter fails with none at zero fuel. At positive fuel it evaluates g(x), sets next=y-eta g(x), returns (x,1) if ||next-x||<=(1-eta)epsilon, and otherwise recurses from next with one less fuel, adding one to a successful count. Counts include the terminal successful test.
For those witnesses and w=((X,P),((zeta0,zeta1),(G0,G1))), define
  P0(w)=a P+sigma zeta0,
  Y0_i(w)=X+t_i P0(w),
  Z0_j(w)=grad V(q(Y0_j(w))+sqrt(eta)G0_j),
  Y1_i(w)=Y0_i(w)-sum_j omega_ij Z0_j(w),
  Z1_j(w)=grad V(q(Y1_j(w))+sqrt(eta)G1_j),
  Phi(w)=(X+h P0(w)-sum_j b_j Z1_j(w),
          a(P0(w)-sum_j d_j Z1_j(w))+sigma zeta1),
  T(w)=2m+sum_i[(N(Y0_i(w))+1)+(N(Y1_i(w))+1)] in N.
Then Phi and T are measurable, and there exists a Markov kernel K from E x E to E x E with, for every incoming state s,
  K(s)=(z -> Phi(s,z))_* gamma.
For every w, one has the exact successful execution identity
  phaseQuery(grad V,eta,epsilon,h,t,omega,b,d,(y -> N(y)+1),w)
    =some(Phi(w),T(w)).
By its approved definition, phaseQuery computes P0,Y0, sequentially collects m calls to run at the first-stage inputs, and maps each successful pair (r,k) to (g(r+sqrt(eta)G0_i),k+1). It constructs Y1 using the first collected gradient array, then sequentially collects the corresponding m second-stage calls, mapping each success to (g(r+sqrt(eta)G1_i),k+1). It returns the displayed final update and sum of collected counts; a failed call propagates none. collectQueries returns empty array/count zero at m=0, otherwise collects the first node and recursive tail and adds counts. Thus the asserted success counts all interpreter tests plus one extra shifted-gradient evaluation per node in each stage, with total overhead exactly 2m. This definition is explicitly linked in the approved context, without any additional theorem premise.
Finally w->(T(w):R) is Bochner integrable under mu and
  integral (T(w):R) dmu(w) <= (m:R)(2+L0+L1).
All sums range over all m actual nodes. The theorem establishes global successful exact-real execution, witness/error/measurability conditions, a probability transition kernel and this total expected abstract gradient-evaluation bound. It asserts no sampler invariant law, convergence, bias, final-state moment bound, finite-precision result, source-specific quadrature contract or wall-clock complexity.

For these witnesses, Phi,T are measurable and a single Markov K has the pushforward equality for every incoming s. The successful phaseQuery identity holds for every full input w, not merely almost everywhere under mu. The integrability and expected count bound concern mu. Hessian hypotheses hold for every x,v; t and row-sum bounds for every node i. m may be zero.
assumptions: 1<=kappa with kappa nonnegative; V is C^2; kappa^(-1)||v||^2<=D^2 V(x)[v,v]<=||v||^2 for all x,v. 0<eta<=c<1,epsilon>0. nu is a probability measure; grad V(xstar)=0; h,M,S>=0. Squared incoming distance from xstar plus squared momentum is integrable with mean <=M. |t_i|<=1 and sum_j |omega_ij|<=S for each node. Final weights b,d are arbitrary real arrays. Gaussian laws are centered identity-covariance independent products. No Gaussian hypothesis on nu, independence between its state coordinates, positive m, or quadrature/order normalization is imposed. phaseQuery semantics is supplied by the approved definition, not an added assumption.
conclusion: There exist global measurable p,q,N with exact implicit equation, epsilon approximation and successful interpreter equality at fuel N(y)+1 for each y. Phi,T are measurable. A Markov kernel K equals the gamma pushforward of Phi at every incoming state. The executable phaseQuery, with g=grad V and fuel(y)=N(y)+1, returns some(Phi(w),T(w)) for every w. The real count T is integrable under mu and its mean is <=m(2+L0+L1). T=2m+sum_i[(N(Y0_i)+1)+(N(Y1_i)+1)] exactly counts all first/second-stage interpreter evaluations and their extra shifted-gradient evaluations.
scopes: Success is pointwise on every full input w; the expected count bound uses the particular incoming law nu independently combined with Gaussian noise. The kernel identity holds for all incoming states. Counts include terminal interpreter tests and the extra first/second-stage shifted-point gradient probes, with overhead 2m. They exclude arithmetic, random generation and elapsed time. The approved context explicitly defines phaseQuery with the paired program body, resolving the former definition-link ambiguity. Fin(m) denotes actual nodes. This conclusion contains no separate per-index moment/count inequalities, final-state moment guarantee, invariant distribution, sampler convergence, numerical-bias estimate or source-specific quadrature guarantee. No material semantic ambiguity remains.
